title: Sparrow mini telemetry pad
content:
Quick scratch sheet for the small microburst runs I'm tracking while debugging cold-start vs warmed-KV behavior. Not formal — just a compact ledger I can scan before standups.

Context: noticing some noisy 95th pct spikes when seq len variation is high and batch packing is inconsistent. Hypothesis: KV cache warming + quantized attention path selection sometimes picks slower kernel for short sequences. Small experiments to correlate: latency vs cache_hit_ratio and batch_util.

Legend / fields: date, run_id, model, seq_len (median), batch_size, quant (bits), cache_state (cold/warm/partial), latency_p50(ms), latency_p95(ms), cost_per_tok_est, notes

Table (compact):
Date | Run | Model | Seq | Batch | Quant | Cache | p50 | p95 | $/tok | Notes
2025-02-12 | r-014 | redwood-v0.9 | 64 | 8 | 4-bit | cold | 42 | 138 | 0.00015 | first cold run after restart, many cache misses
2025-02-12 | r-015 | redwood-v0.9 | 64 | 8 | 4-bit | warm | 22 | 36 | 0.00008 | warmed after steady traffic; consistent
2025-02-17 | r-023 | rw-v1.1-small | 128 | 4 | 8-bit | partial | 48 | 92 | 0.00012 | mixed batch shapes, observed kernel fallback logs (see PR 1298)
2025-02-24 | r-037 | redwood-v0.9 | 32 | 16 | 4-bit | warm | 18 | 34 | 0.00007 | packed well, good tail latency
2025-02-28 | r-045 | redwood-v0.9 | variable (20-300) | 12 | dynamic | partial | 60 | 220 | 0.00020 | big p95 spike, likely due to long sequence routing to non-optimized kernel

Quick observations (notes to self):
- Cache warmup reduces p95 by ~2–4x in these small samples. Need to quantify warmup time vs sustained throughput.
- Mixed sequence workloads spike p95; consider routing policy that isolates long-seq requests to a dedicated lane or preemptive packing.
- PR 1298 has a logging change that helps identify kernel fallbacks; add a flag to log kernel decisions in synthetic runs.
- Cost math: rough cost/tok estimate uses tokens = seq_len * batch, price based on internal unit cost. This is noisy for variable sequences.

Immediate next steps (tiny TODO):
- [ ] Run 1h steady stream (seq=64) to measure warmup curve (record p50/p95 every 5m).
- [ ] Create synthetic mixed workload (20/100/300 ratio 6:3:1) and run 30m to capture kernel selection distribution. Link results to INF-4821.
- [ ] Add small tracepoints in runtime to mark cache_hit_ratio per request (will help correlate).

Reference links:
- INF-4821 (bug + notes)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298 (kernel-fallback logs)
- Slack thread: #eng-serving-runtime (see TS-171304 for early chatter)

Two-minute summary to paste in standup: "Small personal bench: cold cache increases p95 heavily; warm steady traffic looks fine. Mixed seq workloads cause kernel fallback and tail spikes. Doing a controlled warmup and synthetic mix next week to quantify. See my scratch sheet."
